summary: Final Vehicle ladder readout for Auvrelquith Biosciences. The initial screen exposed the limits of clarity at preparation; buffer adjustment then prevented precipitation on dilution and supported selection of a solution for exposure work.

slides.title: AU-08: solution choice for exposure work
slides.subtitle: {{PRJ0105:project_id}} | {{PRJ0105:lims_id}} | Auvrelquith Biosciences | Julia Carver | 06/06/2016 | Durnesswick Laboratories Inc

slides.title: Decision at close
bullets: Auvrelquith Biosciences selected the buffer-adjusted solution for exposure work.
The initial ladder did not establish a stable aqueous solution at target loading.
Selection depends on dilution behavior, not simply on concentrate appearance.

slides.title: Initial Vehicle ladder: loading and physical behavior
Equilibrium capacity is only part of the choice
slides.notes: Target loading 10 mg/mL. This chart does not measure dilution behavior or particle-size distribution.

slides.title: Work package sequence
bullets: Started 04/19/2016; interim discussion 05/13/2016; completed 06/06/2016.
Miguel Serrano developed the formulation set under Julia Carver’s development lead.
Lena Patel supported the exposure-work handoff.

slides.title: Screen design and suitability
bullets: Target loading: 10 mg/mL; compare preparation appearance with the standing condition.
Keep composition, preparation order and identity on the bench sheet.
Equilibrium solubility does not establish a dosing hold time.

slides.title: What the starting formulation set tells us
bullets: Polymer vehicles remained suspensions.
Cyclodextrin improved capacity relative to the citrate-buffer starting point without giving a clear preparation.
bullets_right: The surfactant/cosolvent mixture appeared clear initially.
Precipitate on standing removed clarity as a sufficient selection rule.

slides.title: Dilution is the relevant stress
bullets: A concentrate can look acceptable before its solvent environment changes.
Dilution changes excipient support and the dissolved/solid balance.
AU-08 follow-up therefore focused on buffer condition as well as concentrate preparation.

slides.title: Buffer adjustment: interpretation
bullets: The project follow-up found that buffer adjustment prevented precipitation on dilution.
This is distinct from the starting pH 4 citrate-buffer row.
Do not substitute that starting recipe for the selected exposure recipe.
slides.notes: Adjusted-buffer composition and quantitative dilution measurements are not supplied. Keep the starting screen separate from the successful follow-up.

rows: Do not select on initial clarity
Precipitation prevented on dilution in project follow-up

slides.title: Reading the dilution appearance comparison
bullets: Compare concentrate, diluted preparation and held preparation under consistent viewing conditions.
Keep recipe identity beside each observation.
The outcome here is qualitative; a photograph panel is not reproduced.
slides.notes: The archive description refers to dilution photographs, but no image assets are supplied. Do not replace missing photographs with simulated evidence.

slides.title: Exposure use and process lock
bullets: Use the buffer-adjusted recipe for planned exposure work.
Tie dose concentration in mg/mL to the intended dosing volume.
bullets_right: A commercial process lock is not established.
A changed material lot, loading or dilution medium requires a compatibility check.

slides.title: Transfer instructions
bullets: Lena Patel: carry buffer identity, adjustment order and dilution medium into the recipe card.
Miguel Serrano: retain starting-ladder observations with the bench sheets.
Julia Carver: distinguish follow-up success from the original screen in the handoff.

slides.title: Closeout and next scale gate
bullets: {{PRJ0105:project_id}} is complete; the solution approach has been selected.
Agree hold interval, container and mixing sequence before larger preparation.
Scope reproducibility and material demand before extending beyond exposure work.
